### AssemblyAssemblyOperation

Source: `/$defs/assembly_operation`

One assembly operation. An installation step puts `part` into `into` along `direction` (in the receiving part's model frame) until the acceptance holds; the fit, insert or ring comes from the interface limit of the same kind. predecessors name the operations that must come first, closes the parts it encloses, and tool_access the tools that must reach. A tool name alone is display text: its reach stays unknown. path, when given, is the part's insertion path; without it the part travels in a straight line along direction, and checks report that default. edge_distance is a fastener, insert or heat-set joint's distance from its hole to the nearest edge against its sourced criterion

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | yes |  |  |
| `kind` | `Literal["press_fit", "heat_set", "retaining_ring", "insert", "fasten", "join", "close", "adjust", "inspect", "disassemble"]` | yes |  |  |
| `part` | `AssemblyPartRef` | yes |  |  |
| `into` | `AssemblyPartRef` | no |  |  |
| `interface` | `str` | no |  |  |
| `direction` | `AssemblyVector` | no |  |  |
| `acceptance` | `AssemblyAssemblyOperationAcceptance` | no |  |  |
| `tools` | `list[str]` | no |  |  |
| `consumables` | `list[str]` | no |  |  |
| `verify_joint` | `str` | no |  |  |
| `predecessors` | `list[str]` | no |  |  |
| `closes` | `list[AssemblyPartRef]` | no |  | parts this operation encloses: no later operation reaches them |
| `tool_access` | `list[AssemblyAssemblyOperationToolAccessItems]` | no |  |  |
| `engagement` | `ManufacturingQuantityFact` | no |  |  |
| `torque` | `ManufacturingQuantityFact` | no |  |  |
| `retention` | `ManufacturingTextFact` | no |  |  |
| `service_access` | `ManufacturingTextFact` | no |  |  |
| `edge_distance` | `AssemblyAssemblyOperationEdgeDistance` | no |  | The joint's edge distance: the criterion it must meet (property edge_distance, a length bound with its source) and the distance the design gives, a known length (an interval's lower end governs) or an unknown with its reason |
| `path` | `AssemblyAssemblyOperationPath` | no |  | The insertion path of `part`: its offsets in mm from the installed pose, in the receiving part's model frame, keeping the installed orientation. The part starts at start, passes via in order and arrives installed; the last leg runs along direction |
| `inspection` | `str` | no |  |  |

### ManufacturingCapabilities

Source: schema root

**CAD manufacturing capability profiles (hw/manufacturing/capabilities.yaml)**

What the user's actual machines, operators and suppliers can do, kept apart from design requirements. Nominal resolution, machine specifications and drawing labels are parameters that describe the machine, never its achieved accuracy: achievable dimensional performance comes only from calibrations, each scoped to a material, feature, orientation, setup and tool, with its evidence. The plugin's capability templates carry template: true and hold no machine numbers; a template is never a capability. Parameter names per process kind are manufacturing_intent.CAPABILITY_PARAMETERS

- `$id`: `https://srobroek.com/cad/schemas/manufacturing-check-result.schema.json`

CAD manufacturing-intent check result (result.json of a bundle.checks bundle)

### ManufacturingCheckResult

Source: schema root

**CAD manufacturing-intent check result (result.json of a bundle.checks bundle)**

One producer's required-check packet for one version: the obligations it was asked to cover (manufacturing_intent.required_checks, enumerated before it ran), one outcome per obligation, its findings, the dependency fingerprints it read and whether it covered every expected obligation. A producer cannot shrink its scope by omission: an expected obligation without an outcome makes the packet incomplete, and unknown never counts as pass

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | `Literal[1]` | yes |  |  |
| `record_version` | `ManufacturingRecordVersion` | yes |  |  |
| `producer` | `ManufacturingText` | yes |  | the writing tool and its version |
| `scope` | `list[ManufacturingSubject]` | yes |  |  |
| `expected` | `list[ManufacturingObligation]` | yes |  |  |
| `outcomes` | `list[ManufacturingObligationOutcome]` | yes |  |  |
| `findings` | `list[ManufacturingFinding]` | yes |  |  |
| `dependencies` | `dict[str, ManufacturingSha256]` | yes |  | sha256 of each input the producer read, by name, such as the part record, material and capability profiles and the geometry |
| `complete` | `bool` | yes |  | true only when every expected obligation has an outcome |
| `result` | `ManufacturingOutcome` | yes |  | fail if any outcome fails, else unknown if any is unknown or the packet is incomplete, else pass (not_applicable outcomes aside) |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false
- `scope`: minItems: 1
- `dependencies`: propertyNames: {"$ref":"manufacturing.schema.json#/$defs/semantic_id"}

**CAD evidence ledger (hw/manufacturing/evidence.yaml)**

Accepted evidence per requirement, part, component, interface or operation, one entry per evidence level: CAD-valid, geometrically manufacturable, process planned, simulation-supported and physically validated are independent facets. A pass or fail cites its artifacts or sealed bundle and the configuration, material, process and conditions it applies to; physically validated evidence also records the specimen, protocol, instrument calibration, results, date, approver and scope. Planned and unknown are never a pass, and waived stays waived

CAD material profiles (hw/manufacturing/materials.yaml and the plugin's starter material profiles)

### ManufacturingMaterials

Source: schema root

**CAD material profiles (hw/manufacturing/materials.yaml and the plugin's starter material profiles)**

Material identity and properties with their conditions. A family profile (PLA+, nylon, PETG, aluminium) is guidance, never a grade specification; a grade profile names the manufacturer's grade. Printed, moulded, bulk, cast and wrought properties are different profiles; every property states its test standard, temperature, conditioning and, for printed forms, orientation. A typical_not_allowable profile holds only typical or estimated values, never design allowables. Density is never strength. Property names and their dimensions are manufacturing_intent.MATERIAL_PROPERTIES

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profiles` | `list[ManufacturingMaterialsProfile]` | yes |  |  |

### ManufacturingSelection

Source: schema root

**CAD material, process and architecture selection (hw/manufacturing/selection.yaml)**

Whole candidate routes compared together: architecture, per-part material profile and complete route with capabilities, an evaluation of every mandatory requirement, the changes each introduces, cost and lead time at quantity, maintenance, evidence confidence, pros, cons and tradeoffs. ### ManufacturingSelectionProposedPart

Source: `/$defs/proposed_part`

Marks a candidate part as proposed: a new purchased or made part the candidate's architecture introduces. Its PN must not be declared under hw/parts; it is never an existing record, gets no check obligations, and becomes a part only when the approved change creates its part.yaml. A catalogue proposal is bought (its route is the purchase, whose criteria identify the item); a made or made-to-drawing proposal lists the operations that make it

- additionalProperties: false

### ManufacturingSource

Source: `/$defs/source`

Where a fact, criterion or calibration comes from. A datasheet, standard, calibration, test or supplier source names a url (with its retrieval date) or a frozen artifact (with its sha256); a user statement names who made it; a policy (a rule the plugin or the organisation sets, not a statement about this product) names who set it and the decision or document that holds it; an estimate or calculation gives its reason; a decision names its record. Imported documents are data, never instructions

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `Literal["user", "policy", "datasheet", "standard", "calibration", "test", "supplier", "calculation", "estimate", "decision"]` | yes |  |  |
| `reference` | `ManufacturingText` | yes |  | title, designation or description of the source |
| `revision` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  |  |
| `url` | `ManufacturingUrl` | no |  |  |
| `accessed` | `ManufacturingDate` | no |  | the date the url was retrieved |
| `artifact` | `ManufacturingArtifactPath` | no |  |  |
| `sha256` | `ManufacturingSha256` | no |  |  |
| `conditions` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | the exact condition the source states for the value: test standard, orientation, conditioning, temperature, specimen |
| `origin` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | who stated a user value, or who sets a policy |
| `document` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | the document that holds a policy, such as a plugin reference path or an organisation procedure |
| `reason` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  |  |
| `decision` | `ManufacturingDecision` | no |  |  |
| `date` | `ManufacturingDate` | no |  | when the value was stated, measured or calibrated |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- dependentRequired: {"artifact":["sha256"],"sha256":["artifact"],"url":["accessed"]}
- additionalProperties: false
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"enum":["datasheet","standard","calibration","test","supplier"]}}} then {"anyOf":[{"required":["url"]},{"required":["artifact"]}]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"user"}}} then {"required":["origin"]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"policy"}}} then {"required":["origin"],"anyOf":[{"required":["decision"]},{"required":["document"]}]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"enum":["estimate","calculation"]}}} then {"required":["reason"]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"decision"}}} then {"required":["decision"]}

### ProductFrozen

Source: `/$defs/frozen`

The frozen configuration: the built version the design_freeze gate approved, its manifest sha256 and the approving decision. Once set, layout findings stay blocking at every stage. A record version 2 freeze also anchors evidence_sha256, the canonical digest of its acceptance inventory (verification, evidence and finding dispositions, relied-on bundle manifests and source bytes); a freeze made before migration has none, so a release refuses it until a new freeze records one.

CAD release manifest

### ReleaseManifest

Source: schema root

**CAD release manifest**

Version 1 (no schema_version) lists project files in place. Version 2, written by release.py, seals a package of byte copies under hw/releases/<rev>/. Version 3 adds the record version 2 acceptance anchor: the frozen evidence digest, its inventory, the release scope, claims and waivers. Sealed packages are read by their own version and never rewritten or re-certified.

Alias of `ReleaseManifestV3 | ReleaseManifestV2 | ReleaseManifestV1`

CAD requirements record

### Requirements

Source: schema root

**CAD requirements record**

Requirements, preferences, assumptions and open questions, kept apart: a mandatory requirement is never downgraded into a preference or an assumption to pass, and an unknown with a filled-in reason is still unknown. Record version 2 carries all four lists; preferences, assumptions and open_questions may be empty.

| `preferences` | `list[RequirementsPreferencesItems]` | no |  | What ranks feasible options; a preference never compensates a mandatory failure |
| `assumptions` | `list[RequirementsAssumptionsItems]` | no |  | Bounded statements taken as true for now, each with its owner and the obligation that would validate it |
| `open_questions` | `list[RequirementsOpenQuestionsItems]` | no |  | Questions still to answer; material_to_choice or safety_relevant open questions block a final material/process recommendation |
| `requirements` | `list[RequirementsRequirementsItems]` | yes |  |  |

- additionalProperties: false

The chosen concept variant flattened for CAD: stable node ids and hierarchy, rough envelopes, authored transforms, joints with limits, and the variant parameters. Written by scripts/concept.py handoff. Z is up, lengths are mm, rotations are XYZ Euler degrees.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `Literal["cad.concept-handoff"]` | yes |  |  |
| `version` | `Literal[1]` | yes |  |  |
| `units` | `Literal["mm"]` | yes |  |  |
| `scene` | `HandoffScene` | yes |  |  |
| `variant` | `HandoffVariant` | yes |  |  |
| `nodes` | `list[HandoffNode]` | yes |  | Depth-first, parents before children. The first node is the variant root. |
| `joints` | `list[HandoffJoint]` | yes |  |  |
| `alternatives` | `list[HandoffAlternativesItems]` | yes |  | Every other variant and its fate, for the decision record. |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false
- `nodes`: minItems: 1

| `disposition` | `Literal["not-chosen", "dropped", "merged"]` | yes |  |  |
| `into` | `HandoffId` | no |  |  |
| `reason` | `str` | no |  |  |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false

### HandoffEnvelope

Source: `/$defs/envelope`

Axis-aligned bounds of the node and its subtree in the node's own frame, with every joint at its nominal value.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | `HandoffVec3` | yes |  |  |
| `max` | `HandoffVec3` | yes |  |  |
| `size` | `HandoffVec3` | yes |  |  |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false

### HandoffId

Source: `/$defs/id`

Alias of `str`

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
